baseNote: Chained on the plan-079 branch because this amendment updates plan-079 documents in the same change. Merge order: 079 then 080.
request: Owner: 'Remove rule 1.3 that forbids automating it.'
requestDisposition: Declined as a literal deletion; executed as a re-specification after adversarial review. Reason: the premise was false (section 1.3 banned only automation, while section 1 already permitted manual capture) and deletion alone would have gained no capability while widening the user-contributed provenance class, leaving the rule self-contradicting against its duplicate, and rotting a frozen SHA-pinned verdict.
verifiedConstraints: Section 1.3 never forbade capturing one's own feed; section 1 already permitted it. Only the automation of the transfer was banned.
071/verdict.json records the primary blocker as 'no contributor session available in this environment', citing the rule only as a secondary cause.

No authenticated LinkedIn session is reachable by tooling: no loopback CDP listener, the chrome-devtools MCP browser uses --remote-debugging-pipe, and the owner's Chrome runs without --remote-debugging-port (verified in plan 078).
An agent deleting the rule gains no capability: the operating constraints binding the agent forbid circumvention independently of the repository's text.

plans/research/071/protocol.md: section 1.3 re-specified: manual copy-paste OR single-shot authorized collector (section 1a); still bans unattended collection, bulk extraction, test accounts, credentials
section 1a added: authorized-collector class bounded on nine axes
section 0: user-contributed restated to describe source and consent, not transfer tooling; plan 070's definition explicitly left governing the text corpus only
Forbidden section reconciled with section 1.3 so the two no longer diverge; scope pin and no-raw-capture rule added
new forward-only amendment section with five reversal conditions
changed.plans/research/079/design.md: section 8 no longer cites section 1.3 as the blocker; points at section 1a and plan 080
changed.plans/research/079/verdict.json: notDone entry updated; governanceAmendment block added
changed.plans/research/079/contributor-guide.md: contributor rules unchanged; owner-facing note added pointing at section 1a and plan 080

authorizedCollectorBounds.who: repository owner, acting as the contributor; not a third party, not a second or test account
authorizedCollectorBounds.whoseFeed: the collector's own logged-in feed only
authorizedCollectorBounds.session: already-running, owner-started browser session; no credential handling or storage by tooling, no session export, no private profile copied into an agent-owned browser
authorizedCollectorBounds.invocation: single-shot, human-invoked; one run per explicit owner command
authorizedCollectorBounds.scale: bounded to plan 071 section 3 minimums (>=3 positives, >=2 negatives, >=1 layout variant); no crawling, schedulers, polling, or iteration over routes/profiles/member lists
authorizedCollectorBounds.retention: raw capture lives only in a local scratch file; never committed, attached, or uploaded; deleted once sanitised; only section-2-clean output may be committed
authorizedCollectorBounds.sanitisation: section 2 unchanged plus an independent leak check reporting zero before commit
authorizedCollectorBounds.scopePin: does NOT authorise shipping any collector inside the extension; zero network requests and data_collection_permissions ['none'] must remain true
authorizedCollectorBounds.nonCircumvention: does NOT authorise bypassing authentication, anti-bot systems, CAPTCHAs, access restrictions or rate limits

provenanceSemanticsPreserved.reasoning: user-contributed describes whose feed the capture came from and whose consent it carries, not the tool used to transfer it. An entry produced under section 1a remains user-contributed and still requires real-donated validation (contributor confirms the structure; maintainer confirms sanitisation).

supersededNotEdited.status: frozen, SHA-pinned at baseSha 3aef7b9, NOT edited
supersededNotEdited.why: Its verdict rests on facts that have not changed (realSampleCount 0, cases-real.json [], no contributor session in that environment). section 1.3 was one cited cause among those, not the load-bearing one. Editing it would retro-amend a closed record; the protocol carries a dated superseding note instead.

reversalConditions: Any raw or real capture containing third-party personal data is committed, attached to an issue, or uploaded.
The relaxation is cited to justify anything beyond a single owner-run, own-session, human-invoked capture.
The extension ships or references any network access, contradicting the zero-network and data_collection_permissions ['none'] claims.
An entry enters cases-real.json without a clean independent leak check.
The manual path (section 1) turns out to be sufficient — then the exception was unnecessary and must be removed.

residualRiskAccepted.irreversibleSurface: Public git history. A revert restores the file, but the record of the relaxation — and any capture committed under it — persists and forks retain it.
residualRiskAccepted.mitigation: The retention bound and the leak check exist so that no raw capture ever enters history at all.
residualRiskAccepted.definitionalDrift: Mitigated by restating user-contributed in section 0 as source-and-consent.
residualRiskAccepted.brandRisk: Guarded by the scope pin; tripwired by reversal condition 3.

gateVisibility: The plan-071 gate asserts no protocol prose, so this amendment is invisible to it by design. That is precisely why the change carries a written record and reversal conditions rather than a silent edit.
nextWork: Owner-run: either capture manually per section 1, or run a bounded authorized collector per section 1a, then feed output through plans/research/079/sanitize.cjs (must report zero leaks) before any entry enters cases-real.json.
